did_you_know.text: Did you know? The phrase “to see the daughters of the land” need not mean a passing glance; it can describe going out to meet and get to know the local girls.
Did you know? “To speak to someone’s heart” is a biblical expression for words of comfort, persuasion, or encouragement. Here, it does not erase the wrong done to Dinah.
Did you know? The word “nebalah” here does not mean merely a foolish act; it is a strong word for a disgraceful and morally serious deed.
Did you know? A “mohar” was a marriage payment, while “mattan” referred to additional gifts. Shechem offers to pay whatever is demanded.
Did you know? The word “foreskin” refers to the circumcision connected with the covenant given to Abraham, so Jacob’s sons present circumcision as a condition for joining their group.
Did you know? The phrase “honored above all his father’s household” presents Shechem as a person of high status in his family, not merely as a young man in love with Dinah.
Did you know? In biblical times, the city gate was a central place for gathering, trade, and public decisions. That is why Hamor and Shechem address the townspeople there.
Did you know? In their speech to the townspeople, Hamor and Shechem emphasize livestock and property. This reveals an economic motive for joining the families.
Did you know? “You have troubled me” does not refer to literal murkiness; it means that the brothers have brought danger upon Jacob and made him hated by the people of the land.
Did you know? Simeon and Levi answer with a rhetorical question: they present their actions as defending their sister’s honor, leaving the reader to wrestle with the moral tension.
